# Formatting Style

## Overview

Consistent formatting eliminates a class of review comments that have nothing to do with correctness. This standard defines the authoritative rules for indentation, line length, and whitespace across every language used in DevOS. Linters enforce what they can; this document governs the rest.

## Prescriptive rules

### Rule 1 — Indentation

| Language | Indent unit | Rationale |
|----------|-------------|-----------|
| JavaScript / TypeScript | 2 spaces | Ecosystem default; Prettier, ESLint, and most TS tooling default to 2 |
| Python | 4 spaces | PEP 8; enforced by `black` and `ruff` |
| Bash / Shell | 2 spaces | Keeps nested conditionals readable at typical 80–120 char budgets |
| YAML / JSON | 2 spaces | Standard across most DevOS config files |
| Markdown | 2 spaces (list continuation) | GitHub renderer canonical |

**MUST NOT** use tabs in any source file. Tabs produce inconsistent rendering across editors and git diff viewers.

**MUST NOT** mix indent widths within a single file.

### Rule 2 — Line length

**MUST** keep all source lines ≤ 120 characters.

Exceptions (SHOULD still wrap where readable):
- URLs in comments or documentation
- Long string literals that cannot be split without changing semantics
- Generated code (migration files, lock files, auto-generated JSON)

### Rule 3 — Trailing whitespace

**MUST NOT** leave trailing whitespace on any line. Configure your editor to strip on save. Git pre-commit hooks in this repo enforce this for `.sh`, `.ts`, `.py`, and `.md` files.

### Rule 4 — Final newline

**MUST** end every text file with exactly one newline character. Files missing a final newline cause noisy git diffs and break some POSIX tools.

### Rule 5 — Blank lines

**MUST NOT** use more than 2 consecutive blank lines anywhere in source. One blank line separates logical sections; two blank lines separate top-level declarations. Three or more indicate copy-paste from an editor with different conventions.

## Compliance test

- [ ] Does `command grep -rn ' $' --include='*.sh' --include='*.ts' --include='*.py' scripts/ profiles/ .claude/` return zero results (no trailing whitespace)?
- [ ] Does `command grep -rn $'\t' --include='*.sh' --include='*.ts' --include='*.py' scripts/ profiles/` return zero results (no tabs)?
- [ ] Pick 3 recently edited files and confirm all lines are ≤ 120 characters: `awk 'length > 120 {print FILENAME ":" NR ": " length " chars"}' <file>`

If any check fails: fix before merging. Trailing whitespace and tab/space mixing are always auto-fixable — never justify them inline.
